newsitem.title: USA: Boston Chicken says Q2 sales flat to modestly down.
newsitem.headline: Boston Chicken says Q2 sales flat to modestly down.

text.p: Boston Chicken Inc said it would release details of a restructuring early next week and said second quarter sales so far have been flat to slightly negative. But the restaurant company hopes to turn the sales around into positive territory in the third quarter.
A Boston Chicken spokeswoman told Reuters second quarter sales had been "flat to down modestly". First quarter sales were down about 0.7 to 0.8 percent, she said.

Shares slipped in heavy trading after the company said earlier it was "not satisfied" with current sales momentum. The stock fell nearly 10 percent, off 1-1/8 to 17 in late trading with over 12 million shares traded.

The spokeswoman said Boston Chicken is banking on its strategy of focusing back on dinner, the launching of a new program aimed at kid's meals, and a strategy of value, convenience and quality to turn its sales around. She added the caveat that it was, of course, difficult to predict what would happen in the third quarter.

Earlier, the company said the aggressive discounts it used to build its lunch business had cut into its core business, dinner sales. The spokeswoman, Karen Rugen, said the company was using a "Don't Mess with Dinner" strategy.
She said sales would also be helped because the dinner market is less subject to discounting.
She also said the company had adequate capital to last the company through mid-1998 after it completed a recent $250 million convertible debt offering.

Earlier, the company said it had built up "too many layers" and is working on cutting duplications between area developers and a company support center and streamlining administrative functions. The spokeswoman said details would be released early next week.
An analyst who did not wish to be identified said the company would likely unveil a severance charge.
The changes will not involve employees at the store level, or Einstein/Noah Bagel Corp, which is 53 percent owned by Boston Chicken, the company said.
